basis: Developmental impairment and epilepsy define CNS disease; extracerebral findings in single patients do not establish involvement in >=30% of the broader cohort.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease. Cardiac, GI and skeletal malformations are described as common, supporting ~30% involvement; precise rates unavailable.
Contact lens-associated corneal edema is localized to the eye.
Hypothyroidism, colitis and cardiac hypertrophy define syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 30-79%. Craniosynostosis also occurs in 30-79% but musculoskeletal omitted at cap.
Enteroviral infection umbrella; intestinal replication does not establish common intestinal damage, and neurologic or cardiac disease is subtype-specific.
Muscular dystrophy directly affects skeletal muscle; no evidence establishes additional common organ involvement.
Mesothelioma in situ arises in pleural mesothelium; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Primary tumor arises in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; metastatic or obstructive complications are not defining common organ damage.
Skeletal dysplasia affects limb bones, vertebrae and joints; intelligence is normal and no other organ damage is established.
Papilloma arises in buccal mucosa, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis; an infectious cause is not specified.
Nonsyndromic intellectual developmental disorder with speech impairment; no extracerebral organ disease is established.
Alzheimer neurodegeneration causes cortical atrophy, memory impairment and dementia.
HNF4A-related monogenic diabetes affects endocrine pancreatic function; diabetic end-organ complications are separate diseases.
Defined by impaired central respiratory signaling and recurrent cessation of breathing; associated heart disease and later cardiovascular risks do not qualify.
Bronchiolar inflammation directly affects small airways; most clinical cases are viral infections, commonly RSV.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is common across chromosome 17 partial duplication syndromes; additional organ abnormalities depend on the duplicated segment.
Deep corneal disease associated with anterior scleral inflammation; the supplied concept does not establish an infectious or autoimmune cause.
Primary antibody deficiency; respiratory infections and asthma are separate diagnoses. Bronchiectasis occurs in only 5-29%, below the threshold for pulmonary involvement.
GALM deficiency impairs galactose metabolism; cataracts occur in 30-79%. Cholestasis and impaired liver function occur in only 5-29%.
Defined by hemorrhage into skin or mucosa and classified as a hemorrhagic blood disorder; vessel inflammation or systemic vascular damage is not inherent.
Gestational trophoblastic tumor arises in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; metastatic sites are not intrinsic defining involvement.
Benign smooth-muscle tumor of the uterine corpus; uterine reproductive tissue is outside the axes and is not skeletal muscle.
Posterior staphyloma is an outpouching of the posterior ocular wall involving the sclera.
GM2 storage causes neurodegeneration; visual impairment occurs in 30-79% with retinal involvement. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; aspiration pneumonia is a separate complication.
Impaired writing is defined chiefly by dysfunction or injury of cerebral writing networks; developmental learning impairment also maps to neurologic.
